events.title: Birth of Adolf Hitler
events.description: Adolf Hitler was born in Braunau am Inn, Austria-Hungary. He later became leader of the Nazi Party and dictator of Germany from 1933 to 1945.
events.significance: Hitler's rise to power led to World War II and the Holocaust, one of the deadliest conflicts and worst genocides in human history, reshaping the global political order.

events.title: Marie and Pierre Curie Isolate Radium Chloride
events.description: In their laboratory in Paris, Marie and Pierre Curie succeeded in isolating radioactive salts of radium after years of processing tons of pitchblende.
events.significance: The isolation of radium advanced the understanding of radioactivity, contributed to the development of nuclear physics, and opened the way for radiation therapy in cancer treatment.

events.title: Columbine High School Massacre
events.description: Two students, Eric Harris and Dylan Klebold, killed 12 students and one teacher and wounded many others at Columbine High School in Colorado before taking their own lives.
events.significance: One of the most infamous school shootings in U.S. history, it prompted nationwide debate on gun control, school security, bullying, and mental health, and changed emergency response protocols.

events.title: Deepwater Horizon Oil Rig Explosion
events.description: An explosion on the Deepwater Horizon drilling rig in the Gulf of Mexico killed 11 workers and triggered a massive oil spill that lasted nearly three months.
events.significance: It was the largest marine oil spill in history, causing severe environmental and economic damage along the Gulf Coast and leading to stricter offshore drilling regulations.

events.title: Publication of Edgar Allan Poe's 'The Murders in the Rue Morgue'
events.description: Poe's short story, widely regarded as the first modern detective story, appeared in Graham's Magazine in April 1841, introducing the detective C. Auguste Dupin.
events.significance: The story established conventions of the detective fiction genre that influenced later writers such as Arthur Conan Doyle and Agatha Christie.
